main_text.p: tò evidentius panis terrenus & visi-bilis panem cœlestem ac invisibilem, potus terrenus & visibilis potum invisibilem & cœlestem & nomine & imagine refert.

Hoc nimirū illud ipsum est quod apud Augustinū toties recurrit, Solet res quæ significat, eius rei quā significat, nomine nuncupari. At nequis cogitet, regulam modò positam ad locutiones sacramentales Eucharistiæ præcipuè non pertinere: perpēdat paulò altius quæ idem ille pater de hac consuetu-dine scripturæ sacræ, tam specialiter quàm generaliter, in epistola ad Bo-nifacium admonet, sic scribens: Si sacramenta similitudinem quandam earum rerum quarū sacramenta sunt, non haberent, omnino sacramenta non essent. Ex hacaut similitudine plerunque rerum ipsarum nominā sortiuntur. Sicut ergo secundum quendam modum, sacramentum corporis Christi, corpus Christi est, & sacrametum sanguinis Christi, sanguis Christi est ; ita sacramētum fidei fides est. &c. Porrò significatio quæ ob si-militu-

page.notes: Catchword "militu-" is uncertain: it stands at the bottom right as a hyphenated word and may be a catchword or the last word of the line. "hacaut" is uncertain: the word may be "autem" or an abbreviated form, and I have transcribed it as printed. "nomine" in "nomine nuncupari" and the italic spans are approximate in extent. Printed spellings such as "sacrametum" and "sacramētum" are left as printed.
